findings.summary: Saving a goal now requires an active Connection, which contradicts the product model of owner-only goals on private contacts kept before any friend installs the app, and breaks the evolution order where goals (evolution.2) ship before connections exist (evolution.3).
findings.evidence: New precondition: "Active Connection with the contact's linked account" and S.webapp.due: "A goal may be saved only for a contact with an active Connection". This conflicts with GD.contacts: "Keep a private contact record before any friend installs the app" and GD.goals: "An owner-only goal". Also evolution.3 (Consented pair connections) dependsOn evolution.2 (Goals).

findings.summary: Snooze, pause and revise all go through operation.goal.save, so after a disconnect or block (or for any never-connected contact) an existing goal can no longer be snoozed, paused or revised.
findings.evidence: affordance.SuggestionCard.snooze invokes operation.goal.save. J.prompts/p5, p6 and p7 have stepOperation operation.goal.save. The new failure is "A goal for an unconnected contact is refused", while S.webapp.prompts says blocking "must pause the blocker's corresponding goal".

findings.summary: The operation description and the GoalForm Save failure list were not updated to match the new connection precondition.
findings.evidence: operation.goal.save description still reads "Owned contact and valid interval." affordance.GoalForm.save failure lists only validation and stale-version failures, with no unconnected-contact refusal.
